# Iran says missiles no longer bound by range limits

Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced Saturday that restrictions on ballistic missile range have been lifted, citing Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's directive to respond to threats with "no geographical limits."

IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi stated: "That restriction has been lifted for us," though he did not confirm whether Iran has developed longer-range weapons, asserting instead that capabilities should be demonstrated through action rather than public statements.

Iran has historically maintained a self-imposed 2,000-kilometer range limit on its ballistic missiles, sufficient to reach Israel and U.S. military installations throughout the Middle East. The announcement raises questions about potential strikes against more distant targets if hostilities resume.

The declaration follows previous tensions, including an incident in March when U.S. and British officials reported two ballistic missiles were launched toward Diego Garcia, a joint military base in the Indian Ocean approximately 4,000 kilometers away. British Defence Secretary John Healey stated one fell short and another was intercepted. Iran denied involvement.

Mohebbi warned at an IRGC Aerospace Week conference: "Any point from which we sense a serious threat against our country can become our target," cautioning that future attacks would carry substantial consequences.

The missile program remains central to Iran's military deterrence strategy, particularly after conflicts that degraded conventional capabilities and air defenses.
